checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-1559 base_fee_per_gas correctly validated against parent block parameters?

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could set an incorrect base_fee_per_gas to undercharge for block space.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all P2P entry points where block headers are received and validated. 2. Review the header validation logic that checks base_fee_per_gas against the EIP-1559 formula. 3. Verify that the expected base fee is calculated as: parent_base_fee * (1 + elasticity_multiplier * (parent_gas_used - parent_gas_target) / parent_gas_target / base_fee_max_change_denominator). 4. Attempt to submit blocks with incorrect base_fee_per_gas values: (a) base fee too low when parent block was above gas target, (b) base fee too high when parent block was below gas target, (c) base fee unchanged when it should have adjusted. 5. Verify all malformed blocks are rejected with appropriate error messages. 6. Check edge cases: genesis block handling, first block after fork, maximum/minimum base fee bounds.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Trust Boundary: tb-023, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-004-INV-005. Incorrect base fee calculation could enable spam attacks by underpricing block space or denial of service by overpricing transactions.

checklist.title: Verify Internal Logic: Does the block builder correctly calculate base_fee_per_gas following EIP-1559 rules?

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could set an incorrect base_fee_per_gas to undercharge for block space.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the block construction flow from actor-block-builder to actor-execution-client. 2. Verify that parent block data (base_fee, gas_used, gas_limit) is correctly retrieved from actor-parent-block. 3. Review the base fee calculation implementation for arithmetic overflow/underflow vulnerabilities. 4. Verify that integer division is handled correctly and matches the EIP-1559 specification. 5. Test with boundary values: (a) parent block at exactly gas_target, (b) parent block at gas_limit (full), (c) parent block empty (0 gas used). 6. Verify the elasticity multiplier and denominator constants match EIP-1559 specification.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Supporting nodes: actor-execution-client, actor-block-builder, actor-parent-block. The block builder must correctly implement the EIP-1559 formula to maintain fee market integrity.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas fields validated according to EIP-4844 blob gas accounting rules?

reachability.notes: Incorrect blob gas accounting allows blob spam or underpriced blob transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas are calculated in header construction. 2. Verify that blob_gas_used equals the sum of BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOB (131072) multiplied by the number of blobs in all transactions. 3. Verify that excess_blob_gas is correctly computed using parent's excess_blob_gas and blob_gas_used with TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK. 4. Attempt to construct blocks with mismatched blob counts vs blob_gas_used values. 5. Test edge cases: zero blobs, maximum blobs (6 per block), and boundary conditions. 6. Verify header validation rejects blocks with incorrect blob gas accounting.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Trust Boundary: tb-023, Invariant: blocks-SG-004-INV-006. PoC: demonstrate a block with incorrect blob_gas_used or excess_blob_gas that passes validation.

checklist.title: Verify Execution Client correctly calculates blob gas metrics during block processing

reachability.notes: Incorrect blob gas accounting allows blob spam or underpriced blob transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate blob gas calculation logic in the execution client (actor-execution-client). 2. Trace the data flow from blob transactions to blob_gas_used calculation. 3. Verify the formula: blob_gas_used = num_blobs * BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOB (131072). 4. Test with crafted transactions containing varying blob counts. 5. Verify integer overflow protections in blob gas calculations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Supporting check for actor-execution-client node.

checklist.title: Verify Block Builder enforces EIP-4844 blob limits and gas accounting

reachability.notes: Incorrect blob gas accounting allows blob spam or underpriced blob transactions.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate block building logic in actor-block-builder. 2. Verify that blob transaction selection respects MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (786432). 3. Verify excess_blob_gas calculation follows: max(0, parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used - TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK). 4. Test block building with maximum blob transactions. 5. Verify correct handling when blob gas limit would be exceeded.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Supporting check for actor-block-builder node.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the requests_hash field in block headers correctly computed according to EIP-7685?

reachability.notes: Incorrect requests_hash causes CL-EL disagreement and block rejection at consensus level.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where requests_hash is computed in header construction (SG-004). 2. Verify that compute_requests_hash() implementation strictly follows EIP-7685 specification. 3. Trace the requests data flow from execution to consensus layer across trust boundary tb-017. 4. Attempt to submit blocks via P2P or Engine API with mismatched requests_hash values. 5. Verify that validation layers (Header validation, Requests hash verification) correctly reject blocks with incorrect requests_hash. 6. Test edge cases: empty requests list, maximum requests, malformed request types. 7. Verify CL-EL agreement by comparing requests_hash computation on both sides.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Trust Boundary: tb-017, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-004-INV-007, Source Assumption: asm-041. PoC guidance: demonstrate a block where requests_hash does not match the computed value from the actual requests.

checklist.title: Verify EIP-7685 Request Hash Computation: Are all request types properly included in the hash computation?

reachability.notes: Incorrect requests_hash causes CL-EL disagreement and block rejection at consensus level.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Enumerate all request types covered by EIP-7685 (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations). 2. Verify each request type is correctly serialized before hashing. 3. Test with blocks containing each request type individually and in combination. 4. Verify ordering of requests in hash computation matches specification. 5. Test boundary conditions: first/last request type, request type at limits. 6. Verify that execution client (actor-execution-client) and consensus layer (actor-consensus-layer) produce identical hash for the same request set.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Supporting check for EIP-7685 compliance across CL-EL boundary.

checklist.title: Verify CL-EL Synchronization: Does header validation prevent consensus disagreement from requests_hash mismatch?

reachability.notes: Incorrect requests_hash causes CL-EL disagreement and block rejection at consensus level.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the validation code paths in both execution client and consensus layer. 2. Verify that blocks with invalid requests_hash are rejected before propagation. 3. Test attack scenario: attacker submits block via P2P with valid header but tampered requests_hash. 4. Test attack scenario: attacker uses Engine API to propose block with mismatched requests. 5. Verify error handling: what happens when CL and EL disagree on requests_hash? 6. Check for timing vulnerabilities: can a block be temporarily accepted before full validation? 7. Verify that block finalization cannot proceed with requests_hash inconsistency.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Focuses on consensus-level impact of requests_hash validation failure.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is Block immutability enforced after construction to prevent post-validation tampering?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the Block class/structure and verify it uses slotted_freezable or equivalent immutability mechanism. 2. Trace all P2P entry points where blocks are received and constructed. 3. Verify that after Block construction, the freeze() method (or equivalent) is called immediately. 4. Attempt to mutate Block fields (header, transactions, ommers, withdrawals) after construction and freeze - verify mutations are rejected with appropriate errors. 5. Check for any code paths between block validation and execution where Block objects could be modified. 6. Verify no references to mutable internal data structures are exposed that could bypass immutability. 7. Test race conditions: attempt concurrent modification during the validation-to-execution window.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Trust Boundary: tb-023, Source Assumption: asm-034, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-005-INV-001. PoC requirement: demonstrate that a Block object can be mutated after construction and freeze.

checklist.title: Verify Block Header Immutability: Can the header field be modified after Block construction?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. After constructing and freezing a Block, attempt to modify the header field directly. 2. Attempt to modify nested fields within the header (e.g., parent_hash, state_root, gas_limit). 3. Verify that AttributeError or FrozenInstanceError is raised on mutation attempts. 4. Check if header is stored as a reference that could be modified externally. 5. Verify that Header objects are also frozen when embedded in a Block.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Supporting check for Block header immutability. Compromised header could alter block identity and chain structure.

checklist.title: Verify Block Transactions Tuple Immutability: Can the transactions tuple be modified after Block construction?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. After constructing and freezing a Block, attempt to modify the transactions tuple. 2. Verify that individual transaction elements (Bytes or LegacyTransaction) cannot be replaced or modified. 3. Check if underlying Bytes or LegacyTransaction objects are also immutable after freeze. 4. Attempt to append or remove transactions from the tuple after freeze. 5. Verify deep immutability - nested transaction fields should also be frozen. 6. Test with both raw Bytes transactions and decoded LegacyTransaction objects.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Supporting check for Block transactions immutability. Mutable transactions could allow injection of unauthorized state changes.

checklist.title: Verify Block Ommers Tuple Immutability: Can the ommers tuple be modified after Block construction?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. After constructing and freezing a Block, attempt to modify the ommers tuple. 2. Verify that individual Header elements within ommers cannot be replaced or modified. 3. Check if the nested Header objects within ommers are also frozen. 4. Attempt to append or remove ommer headers after freeze. 5. Verify ommers tuple is enforced as Tuple[Header, ...] type.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Supporting check for Block ommers immutability. Note: ommers are deprecated post-merge but still part of Block structure for compatibility.

checklist.title: Verify Block Withdrawals Tuple Immutability: Can the withdrawals tuple be modified after Block construction?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. After constructing and freezing a Block, attempt to modify the withdrawals tuple. 2. Verify that individual Withdrawal elements cannot be replaced or modified. 3. Check if nested Withdrawal objects are also frozen (index, validator_index, address, amount). 4. Attempt to append or remove withdrawals after freeze. 5. Verify that withdrawal amounts and validator indices cannot be tampered with post-validation. 6. Test with edge cases: maximum withdrawal amount, validator index boundaries.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Supporting check for Block withdrawals immutability. Compromised withdrawals could lead to unauthorized ETH transfers from validators.

checklist.title: Verify slotted_freezable Implementation: Is the freeze mechanism correctly implemented and resistant to bypass?

reachability.notes: Blocks arrive via P2P. Mutability after construction could allow post-validation tampering.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Examine the slotted_freezable decorator/mechanism implementation. 2. Verify that __setattr__ is overridden to prevent modifications after freeze. 3. Check for bypass methods: (a) object.__setattr__(block, 'header', new_header), (b) direct __dict__ manipulation, (c) __slots__ direct access. 4. Verify that freeze is irrevocable - no unfreeze method exists. 5. Test edge cases: subclassing Block, pickling/unpickling frozen blocks, deepcopy operations. 6. Verify that all Block subclasses also inherit immutability constraints. 7. Test with ctypes or other low-level Python mechanisms that might bypass attribute protection.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0016, Internal supporting check - verifies the correctness of the slotted_freezable immutability mechanism itself. A bypass here would compromise all Block immutability guarantees.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the ommers field validated to be empty for all post-merge (PoS) blocks received via P2P?

reachability.notes: A peer could transmit a block with non-empty ommers to exploit clients that don't validate this post-merge.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P block ingestion handler where blocks are received from peers (trust boundary tb-023, tb-026). 2. Locate the block validation logic that checks the ommers field for post-merge blocks. 3. Verify that a check exists ensuring len(block.ommers) == 0 for all blocks after The Merge. 4. Confirm the validation occurs BEFORE the block is processed, stored, or propagated. 5. Construct a test post-merge block with non-empty ommers tuple containing valid-looking Header objects. 6. Submit the malformed block via P2P and verify immediate rejection with appropriate error (e.g., 'non-empty ommers in post-merge block'). 7. Verify peer scoring/reputation is penalized for sending invalid blocks. 8. Test edge cases: (a) block at exact merge boundary, (b) block with single ommer, (c) block with maximum ommers count from pre-merge era. 9. Verify that pre-merge blocks (if still processed) correctly allow non-empty ommers.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0017, Trust Boundary: tb-023, tb-026, Source Invariant: blocks-SG-005-INV-002, Source Assumption: asm-035. PoC: construct a post-merge block with non-empty ommers and demonstrate it passes validation. Severity elevated to Critical due to attacker_controlled=true at boundary.

checklist.title: Verify Block Builder and Execution Client enforce empty ommers during post-merge block construction

reachability.notes: A peer could transmit a block with non-empty ommers to exploit clients that don't validate this post-merge.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate block construction code paths in actor-block-builder and actor-execution-client. 2. Verify that the block builder NEVER populates the ommers field for post-merge blocks. 3. Verify the ommers field is initialized as an empty tuple () during construction. 4. Check if any external inputs (e.g., Engine API payloads) could inject ommers into block construction. 5. Verify that if an attacker-controlled builder attempts to propose a block with ommers, the execution client rejects it. 6. Test that the execution client does not process uncle/ommer rewards post-merge. 7. Verify no code paths exist that could accidentally add ommers during block assembly.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0017, Supporting check for actor-execution-client and actor-block-builder nodes. Covers: SG-005 (block_construction). Accepting blocks with ommers in PoS violates protocol invariants and could enable reward manipulation.
